hints: Focus on counting bonds, not molecules. Write out $\text{PCl}_5 \rightarrow \text{PCl}_3 + \text{Cl}_2$ and ask yourself how many $\text{P-Cl}$ bonds are lost and what new bond appears.
Notice that $\text{PCl}_5$ has five $\text{P-Cl}$ bonds but $\text{PCl}_3$ keeps three of them, so you are really breaking two $\text{P-Cl}$ bonds to make one $\text{Cl-Cl}$ bond.
Use $\Delta H$ = energy in to break bonds minus energy out to make bonds, and remember that breaking more than you make means the overall change must be positive.
walkthrough:
**Write the equation and picture the bonds**

Think like a builder taking things apart and rebuilding. Breaking bonds needs energy in, making bonds gives energy out.

$$\text{PCl}_5(g) \rightarrow \text{PCl}_3(g) + \text{Cl}_2(g)$$

**Count bonds broken and bonds formed**

$\text{PCl}_5$ contains 5 $\text{P-Cl}$ bonds. Products contain 3 $\text{P-Cl}$ bonds in $\text{PCl}_3$ plus 1 $\text{Cl-Cl}$ bond in $\text{Cl}_2$.

Net change: break 2 $\text{P-Cl}$ bonds, make 1 $\text{Cl-Cl}$ bond.

**Apply the bond energy formula**

Use this friendly rule:
$$\Delta H = \Sigma(\text{bonds broken}) - \Sigma(\text{bonds formed})$$
Energy broken = $2 \times 330 = +660 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Energy formed = $1 \times 242 = 242 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

$$\Delta H = 660 - 242 = +418 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
Positive means endothermic, which makes sense because heating is needed to decompose $\text{PCl}_5$.

options.A: Incorrect. This is the exact reverse of the correct calculation, $242 - 660 = -418$. It comes from using $\Delta H$ = formed minus broken instead of broken minus formed.
options.B: Incorrect. $-88$ comes from two mistakes at once: counting only one $\text{P-Cl}$ bond ($330 - 242 = +88$) and then reversing the sign. You must break two $\text{P-Cl}$ bonds, not one.
options.C: Incorrect. $+88$ comes from $330 - 242$. This counts only one $\text{P-Cl}$ broken. Remember $\text{PCl}_5$ loses two Cl atoms to become $\text{PCl}_3$, so two $\text{P-Cl}$ bonds are broken.
options.D: Correct. Two $\text{P-Cl}$ bonds broken cost $2 \times 330 = 660 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, one $\text{Cl-Cl}$ bond formed releases $242 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. $\Delta H = 660 - 242 = +418 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, endothermic as expected for thermal decomposition.
